angle: Accessibility isn’t just compliance—it’s conversion, loyalty, and market reach.
sourceTitle: Putting sign language AI into users’ hands
linkedinPost:
Accessibility is often framed as cost. It’s actually growth you can count.

Google DeepMind shared new sign-language-to-text capabilities aimed at Deaf and hard of hearing users. Beyond the tech, there’s a straightforward enterprise lesson: accessibility features convert underserved demand into measurable revenue and loyalty.

From shipping AI in customer channels, here’s what changes outcomes:
- Treat accessibility as a first-class acceptance criterion, not a backlog item.
- Instrument the journey: measure deflection from phone to self-serve, NPS uplift among affected users, and completion rates.
- Co-design with the community. Pilots built with real users scale; lab demos don’t.

My take: If you can tie an accessibility feature to reduced handle time, higher conversion, or expanded reach, the business case writes itself—and keeps getting renewed.

If your AI roadmap doesn’t have an accessibility line with owner, metrics, and budget, you’re leaving money (and customers) on the table.

What’s one accessibility improvement you could ship this quarter and measure in dollars? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
